questions.question: Two forces of equal size act on a toy car in opposite directions. What term describes these forces?
options: Unbalanced
Resultant
Balanced
Gravitational

questions.question: A box is pulled to the right with a force of 10 N and pulled to the left with a force of 4 N. What is the resultant force acting on the box?
options: 14 N to the right
6 N to the right
6 N to the left
14 N to the left

questions.question: If all the forces acting on a moving skateboard are completely balanced, what will happen to its speed?
options: It will instantly stop.
It will gradually slow down.
It will speed up.
It will remain at a constant speed.

questions.question: A tug-of-war rope experiences a 150 N force to the left and a 200 N force to the right. In which direction does the resultant force act?
options: To the right, because it is the direction of the larger force.
To the left, because it is the direction of the smaller force.
Upwards, because the forces cancel each other out.
Downwards, because gravity is acting on the rope.

questions.question: How does the size of the resultant force on a cart affect its change in speed?
options: A greater resultant force causes a slower change in speed.
A greater resultant force causes a faster change in speed.
The size of the resultant force has no effect on the rate of speed change.
A smaller resultant force causes a faster change in speed.

questions.question: What is friction?
options: A force that acts only in a vacuum to speed up objects.
A force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another.
A force that pulls all objects toward the centre of the Earth.
A force that only exists when an object is heated.

questions.question: Why are substances like oil or grease added between two moving metal parts?
options: To increase the friction so they grip better.
To reduce the friction between the surfaces.
To increase the weight of the metal parts.
To prevent any forces from acting on the parts.

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure forces?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Joules (J)
Newtons (N)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: What is the main difference between categoric and continuous variables?
options: Categoric variables come in distinct types, whereas continuous variables can take any value on a numerical scale.
Categoric variables are only measured in seconds, whereas continuous variables have no units.
Categoric variables can take any numerical value, whereas continuous variables come in distinct types.
Categoric variables are always kept the same, whereas continuous variables are always changed.

questions.question: In a fair test, how many variables should we actively change to see their effect?
options: None of them
Only the variable we are testing
At least two different variables
All variables except the one we are testing

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of contact forces?
options: They only act when objects are touching.
They can act when objects are far apart in space.
They never slow down or speed up an object.
They do not require any physical contact to push or pull.

questions.question: How do non-contact forces differ from contact forces?
options: Non-contact forces only work when objects are in direct physical contact.
Non-contact forces can act with or without the objects touching.
Non-contact forces cannot cause any change in speed.
Non-contact forces only exist in liquid environments.

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A non-contact force that pulls objects toward the ground.
A contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases.
A force that acts only when an object is at rest.
A force that increases the speed of objects moving through a vacuum.

questions.question: According to the scientific principle of conservation of energy, what is true about energy?
options: Energy can be created but never destroyed.
Energy can be destroyed but never created.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
Energy can be both created and destroyed at will.

questions.question: In a force diagram, what does the length of a force arrow represent?
options: The duration of time the force acts.
The size of the force.
The mass of the object experiencing the force.
The speed of the object.

questions.question: If two rolling balls are moving at the same speed, why is the heavier ball harder to stop?
options: Because the motion of heavier objects is harder to stop.
Because heavier objects have less gravity acting on them.
Because heavier objects experience zero friction.
Because heavier objects have less mass.

questions.question: In physics, what is a force?
options: A type of energy stored in batteries.
A push or a pull.
The speed at which an object travels.
The amount of matter inside an object.
